entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Mr. K.C. Tripathy, Advocate
 -versus-
 State of Odisha .... Opp. Party
 Mr. A.K. Nayak, Advocate for the Opid
 Coram:
 Justice Chittaranjan Dash
 Order
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and the State.

2. This is an application for bail U/s.438 Cr.P.C. filed by the Petitioner in apprehension of arrest for his alleged involvement in the offences U/s.420/450 IPC in connection with Berhampur Town P.S.
Case No.107 of 2016 corresponding to G.R. Case No.5 of 2016 pending in the court of learned Special ADJ-cum-Presiding Officer, Ganjam, Berhampur.
3.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the Petitioner that pursuant to the direction of this court the sum of Rs.4,65,300/- has been deposited as against the outstanding towards the deposit allegedly retained with the company.
He further submitted that the Final form in the case has already been submitted.

4. The learned Counsel also drew the attention of this Court that Section 7 of the OPID Act mandates for a compounding of offence // 2 // before and after institution of the prosecution, however,
subject to the leave of the court in seisin over the matter.

5. Keeping in view the above fact while this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail, it is directed that if the Petitioner chooses to surrender before the learned court below in seisin over the matter within three weeks hence and move for bail, the learned court below shall consider the application of the Petitioner keeping in view the fact that the money in question has since been Santosh Kumar Panda vs State Of Odisha ....
